key_insight: Chronicle is an explainable transformer that learns from full, irregular cancer care timelines to generate continuously updated risk predictions across many cancer types and outcomes.
clinical_relevance: By using hospital-wide longitudinal data, it may help clinicians better stratify prognosis, anticipate adverse events, and support individualized treatment decisions across different healthcare systems.
method: Trained on 53.7 million longitudinal data points from 51,711 patients across 67 cancer types
Models entire patient trajectories natively, without imputation, and predicts eight clinical endpoints in one framework
Uses explainability to attribute each risk update to patient-specific clinical factors over time
evidence_signal: In the abstract, Chronicle outperformed snapshot-based models for overall survival (C-index 0.84 vs 0.76-0.79), achieved AUC 0.80-0.92 for seven adverse event/transfusion endpoints, and generalized to 69,341 external patients across Germany, Switzerland, and the United States.
watch_item: Although promising, performance, calibration, and workflow fit may vary by site and need local validation and careful integration before real-world use.
paper_title: An explainable transformer model learning from entire treatment timelines for pan-cancer risk profiling across healthcare systems
